messages:
maya: Quick heads-up: while testing the new JS SDK prefetcher with client-side leaky-bucket, the sampleapp spikes and we hit 429s from the hosted API. Not a full repro yet but consistent on CI when window=4 and burst=10.

rafael: can you paste the relevant logs? curious if it's client-side burst or server-side quota enforcement kicking in.

maya: logs show a bunch of concurrent requests from prefetch and a short-lived increase in tokens used by the leaky-bucket refill. Server responds with HTTP 429 and `x-retry-after` header sometimes, other times it's 429 without header. snippet:

```
[12:34:01] prefetch: enqueue cursor=curA
[12:34:01] request: GET /v1/pages?cursor=curA
[12:34:01] leakyBucket: consumed=10 available=0
[12:34:02] server: 429 Retry-After=1
[12:34:02] retry scheduled after 1s
[12:34:02] request: GET /v1/pages?cursor=curB
[12:34:02] server: 429 (no header)
[12:34:03] client: backoff jitter applies
```

jin: Two quick thoughts: 1) SDK should prefer `Retry-After` header when present and use server-suggested window. 2) If header is missing, we should fall back to an adaptive smoothing window based on recent 429 frequency (avoid blind exponential backoff that blocks prefetch forever).

maya: agree. Also noticed our sampleapp prefetch aggressively schedules next pages even when prior prefetch retries are pending. That makes bursts repeat.

rafael: For parity, Go and Python SDKs have slightly different behaviors: Go uses server `Retry-After` strictly, Python uses a small local jittered backoff when header absent. We should standardize.

jin: Proposed plan: 1) implement prioritized handling of `x-retry-after` / `Retry-After` headers in JS SDK; 2) add an adaptive smoothing fallback (e.g., baseDelay = 200ms * min(1 + recent429Rate, 10)) when header absent; 3) change prefetch to limit concurrent in-flight prefetches = max(prefetchWindow - inFlightRetries, 1).

maya: sounds reasonable. Also add a visible metric in the console for `client.prefetch_inflight` and `client.429_rate` so onboarding sees why they hit quotas.

rafael: can we also add a flag `paginator.rateStrategy = "server-first" | "client-adaptive"` so customers can tune behavior during migration? Keep default to server-first.

jin: yep. We'll add the flag as opt-in to avoid surprising existing apps. We'll include an integration test that fakes missing Retry-After header and asserts smoothing backoff behavior.

ci-bot: sampleapp CI job #5172 started

maya: next steps: jin to open PR with header parsing + fallback algorithm, rafael to update sampleapp prefetch logic + add metrics, docs-bot to draft a short note for SDK parity for migration guidance.

docs-bot: Draft created: docs/sdks/prefetch-backoff.md (internal)

rafael: tagging @maya for tests. I'll also run a soak with window=6 and burst=20 to surface edge cases.

maya: thanks all. i'll keep this thread for follow-ups and will paste CI traces if the soak shows anything new.
